# ethereum-optimism/optimism Weekly Report (Apr 26 - May 2, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on the technical maturation of the Karst hardfork and the integration of Interoperability (Interop) components across the stack. Significant progress was made in aligning the Rust-based Kona node with `op-node` behavior, specifically through the implementation of NUT bundles for fork activation. The project also achieved a major milestone in core stack cleanup by removing deprecated `ProtocolVersions` support, while simultaneously expanding the `op-deployer` to support ZK and SuperFault dispute games.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Hardfork Integration & Kona Evolution
The transition toward the Karst hardfork saw heavy development, particularly in ensuring parity between Go and Rust implementations.
*   **NUT Bundle Integration:** Kona now executes NUT bundles at Karst activation, with `kona-hardforks` utilizing a new build script to ingest configuration data at compile time ([#20157](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20157)).
*   **Precompile Optimization:** The `bn256Pairing` precompile input size was reduced to improve efficiency for the Karst fork ([#20250](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20250)).
*   **Protocol Refactoring:** A major cleanup effort was completed, removing deprecated `ProtocolVersions` support across `op-alloy`, `kona`, and `op-reth` ([#20317](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20317)).

### Interoperability & Superchain Infrastructure
Work continued on the foundational layers of the Superchain, focusing on cross-chain message safety and monitoring.
*   **Cycle Detection:** Kona's `MessageGraph` now includes cycle detection to prevent circular dependencies in cross-chain messages, matching `op-supernode` logic ([#20303](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20303)).
*   **Supernode Observability:** Introduced Prometheus metrics for `op-supernode` to enhance diagnostic capabilities for node operators ([#20242](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20242)).
*   **Migration Validation:** The new `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator` contract was introduced to verify L1 configurations following interop migrations ([#19946](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19946)).

### Dispute Games & Deployment Tooling
The fault proof ecosystem and deployment automation received several upgrades.
*   **ZK & SuperFault Support:** `op-deployer` was updated to support `GameTypeZKDisputeGame` and ABI encoding for OPCM V2, alongside new outputs for SuperFaultDispute games ([#20219](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20219), [#20403](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20403)).
*   **Challenger Refinements:** `op-challenger` now supports aging game inputs in `run-trace` to better simulate real-world dispute scenarios ([#20252](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20252)).

### Node Stability & Performance
*   **P2P Robustness:** Added a signer grace period to `op-node` to handle L1 unsafe block signer rotations without verification failures ([#20063](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20063)).
*   **Interop Filtering:** Performance enhancements were merged for `op-interop-filter`, including block prefetching during ingestion to prevent stalls on restart ([#20398](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20398)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **L2CM Milestones:** Successfully closed several issues related to the L2 Contracts Manager (L2CM), including audit finding resolutions ([#20102](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20102)) and bundle canonicalization ([#19307](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19307)).
*   **Node Reliability:** Resolved a critical issue where `op-interop-filter` would stall due to unbounded backward scans ([#20362](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20362)).
*   **Reth Snapshots:** Completed the request to provide `op-reth` snapshots on `datadirs.optimism.io` for verifiers ([#18473](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18473)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Reth Storage Format:** A new issue highlights panics in `op-reth` proof initialization when syncing with older v1 storage formats ([#20394](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20394)).
*   **Flaky Tests:** `TestReorgUnsafeHead` ([#20198](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20198)) and `TestStorageProofUsingSimpleStorageContract` ([#20376](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20376)) remain active concerns for CI stability.
*   **Interop Activation:** Detailed planning is underway for the Interop activation hardfork, focusing on block height triggers and dependency set behaviors ([#20402](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20402)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week showed strong cross-stack coordination, particularly between the Go and Rust teams to ensure the Kona node remains a viable alternative to `op-node`. There was significant activity surrounding the L2CM (L2 Contracts Manager) with a focus on retroactive improvements and invariant definitions, suggesting a collaborative push toward hardening the contract management layer. The introduction of support for Moonwell in the Superchain ERC20 Bridge ([#20386](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20386)) indicates ongoing ecosystem expansion and integration with external DeFi protocols.
